title: Ten-Metric Rubric Map
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Open Educational Resources
description: Explore the structure of the ten-metric rubric as a tree, then click the metric that each of ten teacher complaints tests.

learningObjectives: The learner will attribute each of ten teacher complaints to the one rubric metric it tests, with at least 9 of 10 correct on the first attempt.
prerequisites: The ten rubric metrics and the quality and reusability dimensions

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore a tree, then attribute problems to its nodes
keyQuestions: What is broken in this complaint?
Which metric asks the question that this complaint raises?
commonMisconceptions: Readability and accessibility are the same metric
Open license and metadata both describe the license
A resource that is free to read is portable
assessmentOpportunities: "A screen reader reads the picture names as image1.png." Which metric?
"I cannot tell whether I may translate this." Which metric?
Are readability and accessibility the same metric?

controls.name: Explore and Quiz me buttons
controls.description: switch modes. Quiz me starts a new run.

controls.name: Nodes
controls.description: click a node. The same nodes are reachable by keyboard through a hidden list of buttons, and a screen reader announces each node.

controls.name: +, minus, and Fit
controls.description: zoom the map. The map does not zoom with the mouse wheel, so it never captures page scrolling. Once zoomed in, drag to pan.

controls.name: Next
controls.description: moves to the next complaint. Play again repeats the quiz.
